title: The Spirit and the Church
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The Spirit and the church teaches that the Holy Spirit gathers, indwells, gifts, unifies, empowers, and sends the people of God. The church is God’s dwelling place by the Spirit.
summary: The Spirit and the church teaches that the Holy Spirit gathers, indwells, gifts, unifies, empowers, and sends the people of God. The church is God’s dwelling place by the Spirit.
christFocus: Christ builds His church by the Spirit. The Spirit joins believers to Christ’s body, equips them for service, and empowers the church to worship, grow, and bear witness to Jesus.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The church is not merely an organization, event, or building. God’s people are joined to Christ and to one another by the Spirit, becoming a dwelling place for God.

The Spirit gives unity to the church. Believers are one body because they share one Spirit, one Lord, one faith, and one hope. This unity must be guarded with humility and love.

The Spirit also equips the church through gifts, teaching, prayer, fellowship, worship, and mission. Church life is meant to be Spirit-dependent, Scripture-shaped, and centered on Christ.

The Spirit strengthens the church in suffering and mission. The early church walked in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, multiplying as God worked among them.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often treat church as optional, consumer-based, or merely institutional. This doctrine reminds believers that the church is a spiritual people indwelt and built by God.

It also speaks hope to the church-hurt. The failures of people do not erase Christ’s love for His church or the Spirit’s work among God’s people.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Participate in the life of the church as one who belongs to Christ’s body. Seek unity, use your gifts, pray, worship, receive the Word, and serve others. Do not reduce church to attendance or preference; see it as the Spirit-formed people of God.
